Create the files for an operator written in R

Source: R/scaffold.R
use_operator.Rd

Writes a starting point for an operator: an R script that runs a Manager, a Dockerfile to build it into an image, and the Kubernetes manifests to install it (CustomResourceDefinition, RBAC and Deployment).

Usage

use_operator(
  path,
  name,
  group,
  kind,
  version = "v1",
  plural = NULL,
  namespace = "default",
  image = NULL,
  replicas = 1L,
  rk8s_source = "github",
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Directory to write into (created if needed).

name

Operator name, used for the Deployment, ServiceAccount, RBAC objects and the leader election Lease. Lowercase letters, digits and -.

group

API group of the custom resource, e.g. "example.com".

kind

Kind of the custom resource, e.g. "Site".

version

API version of the custom resource.

plural

Plural resource name (default: lowercase kind + "s").

namespace

Namespace to install the operator into.

image

Image name for the Deployment (default "<name>:dev").

replicas

Number of operator replicas; with more than one, leader election keeps a single active one.

rk8s_source

Where the image gets rk8s from: "github" (the default) or the path to a source tarball built with R CMD build, which is copied next to the Dockerfile.

overwrite

Replace existing files.

Value

The paths written, invisibly.

Details

The generated controller watches a new custom resource and, for each object, keeps a ConfigMap it owns holding the object's spec and records status.observedGeneration. Replace the body of reconcile() with your own logic, and extend the RBAC rules if it manages other resources.

Files written (relative to path):

  • operator.R: the controller. It connects in-cluster when run in a pod and through your kubeconfig otherwise, so you can run it locally with Rscript operator.R while developing.

  • Dockerfile: builds the image on rocker/r-ver.

  • deploy/crd.yaml, deploy/rbac.yaml, deploy/deployment.yaml.

Then:

docker build -t my-operator:dev .
kubectl apply -f deploy/

(with kind, run kind load docker-image my-operator:dev before applying).

Examples

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "site-operator")
use_operator(dir, name = "site-operator", group = "example.com", kind = "Site")
list.files(dir, recursive = TRUE)
#> [1] "Dockerfile"             "deploy/crd.yaml"        "deploy/deployment.yaml"
#> [4] "deploy/rbac.yaml"       "operator.R"
